methods.title: Population integrity, control totals and reconciliations
methods.original_automation_ids: AUTO-001 AUTO-002 AUTO-003 AUTO-004 AUTO-005 AUTO-008 AUTO-011 AUTO-016 AUTO-022 AUTO-031
methods.standards_to_verify: ISA 500, 510; source import contracts
methods.question: What reconciliation proves transfer integrity, and what independent evidence addresses completeness?

methods.title: Materiality and clearly trivial thresholds

methods.title: Sampling frame and reproducible selection
methods.standards_to_verify: ISA 500, 530; approved sampling policy
methods.question: Which unit/probability frame does each selector implement?
methods.research_steps: Compare random, systematic, haphazard, targeted, stratified and value-weighted approaches for actual offering. | Research algorithm version, deterministic replay, random-byte-to-index bias, unit deduplication, ordering and seed governance. | Specify treatment of selected high-value items, negative/zero monetary units and changed populations.
methods.input_contract: Approved population/version; unique unit ID; design; strata; seed/random source; algorithm version.
methods.independent_expected_work: Independently enumerated tiny frames validate eligibility, unit uniqueness and deterministic replay; technical distribution/bias checks are proportionate to algorithm. Changing source creates a new design.
methods.unsupported_or_judgment: Reproducible HMAC selection is not itself proof of a statistical sampling plan, independence assumptions or confidence evaluation.
methods.lead_role: Accounting/audit methodology analyst + owning domain engineer
methods.profile: Reproducible simple random selection without replacement
methods.inputs: Stable ordered unique eligible IDs; frame hash; n; entropy/seed; exact existing selector version; specific/excluded strata.
algorithm: Keep current HMAC/rejection/partial-Fisher-Yates implementation and its inputs
Partition specific, residual and excluded units disjointly
Draw n unique residual units without replacement; retain exact order and input basis
Extensions retain earlier selected prefix and tested-unit lineage under the same frame; changed frame requires new design
methods.judgment: Audit objective, unit and design appropriateness require review. Reproducibility is not assurance.
methods.example: Residual IDs A,B,C; n=3 -> all three exactly once. n=4 is invalid. Same pinned selector inputs reproduce its actual order.

methods.title: Audit sample-size determination
methods.standards_to_verify: ISA 530; approved original statistical references and firm policy
methods.question: Which sample-size approach is justified for controls or substantive testing?
methods.research_steps: Research assumptions for population, expected error/deviation, tolerable misstatement/deviation, sampling risk and finite frame. | For selected statistical methods obtain original formula/table/model and explain distributional assumptions; compare independent reference values. | For nonstatistical design document human rationale and factors; specify full-population escalation and unsupported combinations.
methods.input_contract: Purpose; population; risk; expected error; tolerable amount/rate; strata; reliance; selected method.
methods.independent_expected_work: Independent reference table or separately coded computation over approved parameter grid; monotonicity and impossible-risk/size cases. Manual size retains rationale and reviewer.
methods.unsupported_or_judgment: Generic opinion-poll sample-size formulas or n=30 rules cannot substitute for an audit method. No unsourced confidence claims.
methods.lead_role: Accounting/audit methodology analyst + owning domain engineer
methods.profile: Bounded attribute size helper + evidenced substantive-size route
methods.inputs: N where finite; tolerable deviation p; sampling risk alpha; acceptance count c; expected-deviation rationale; statistical design.
algorithm: For binomial zero-acceptance c=0 use smallest integer n with (1-p)^n<=alpha
For general c use smallest n with cumulative Binomial(n,p) at c<=alpha; expected deviation informs the approved acceptance design, not a hidden formula
For finite simple random sampling use exact hypergeometric cumulative probability at the declared minimally unacceptable defect count; record threshold rounding
Substantive/MUS sizes require a separately evidenced matching design/evaluation method; do not apply attribute formulas to money
methods.judgment: Selected risk, tolerable deviation, acceptance plan and adequacy are professional methodology decisions; this helper is a proposed bounded design.
exceptions: Expected deviations incompatible with zero-acceptance plan
Monetary projection requested from attribute plan
methods.example: Fictional binomial alpha=.05,p=.05,c=0 gives n=59; .95^58>.05 and .95^59<=.05.

methods.title: Projection, sampling evaluation and risk allowance
methods.standards_to_verify: ISA 530, 450; selected sampling methodology

methods.input_contract: Approved design; all selected/tested units; audited values; error types; strata; specifics; currency.
methods.independent_expected_work: Independent ratio example: eligible CU1,000, sampled CU200, signed error CU10 gives total CU50 only under approved ratio assumptions; do not add same CU10 again. Test zero/mixed-sign/untested/strata cases.

methods.lead_role: Accounting/audit methodology analyst + owning domain engineer

methods.inputs: Current reconciled residual frame; tested book/audited amounts; selected projection profile; separately tested specifics; strata.

Under existing positive-book same-direction ratio profile compute inclusive residual estimate = residualBook x sampledSignedError / sampleBook
Incremental projection = inclusive estimate - sampled factual errors; retain factual errors separately
Sum disjoint strata/specific effects once; record sampling-risk evaluation and additional work independently; no invented confidence bound
methods.judgment: Projection method, anomaly classification, sampling-risk allowance and acceptable audit basis require methodology review.
methods.example: 1000 CU residual,200 sampled,10 error ->50 inclusive,40 incremental+10 factual. Separate specific error10 ->60 CU total.

Calculate actual-expected difference and ratio under explicit sign/denominator definitions
Freeze substantive expectation/precision/threshold before observed comparison
Generate distinct investigation cases with actual explanation and corroboration; preserve historical explanations on refresh

methods.question: Which physical/recorded unit and timing bridges are required?
methods.research_steps: Research count attendance, floor-to-sheet/sheet-to-floor, location/ownership, third-party stock and count-date roll-forward/back. | Specify quantity units, transfers in transit, count adjustments, receipts/issues, duplicate count sheets and signs. | Separate count existence/condition work from costing and NRV.
methods.input_contract: Item/location/lot; count records; units; movements; ownership terms; period dates.
methods.independent_expected_work: Independent count at different date, transfer between sites, negative count adjustment and consignment; quantity bridge before valuation.
methods.unsupported_or_judgment: A reconciled inventory file or uploaded count sheet is not evidence that attendance and physical procedures occurred.
methods.lead_role: Accounting/audit methodology analyst + owning domain engineer
methods.inputs: Item/location/unit; opening quantity; dated receipts/issues/transfers; signed count; count date/report date; ownership evidence.
algorithm: Reconcile quantity opening +in -out =closing by item/location/unit
Compare actual signed count with register and record both-direction test evidence
Roll counts forward/back with actual intervening movements
Link transfers at both locations and investigate timing/ownership/cut-off rather than treating internal movement as purchase/sale
methods.judgment: Attendance, count instructions, ownership, consignment and reliability remain actual audit work.
exceptions: Count date differs from report date
methods.example: Opening10+receipts5-issues8=closing7 units;count6 ->register overstatement1 unit before valuation.

methods.title: Inventory cost and cost of sales
methods.standards_to_verify: IAS 2 or separate SME inventory sections; approved accounting policy
methods.question: Which cost formula and overhead treatment apply to each inventory class?
methods.research_steps: Research specific identification, FIFO and weighted average applicability, consistency and periodic versus perpetual calculations. | Specify purchase/conversion costs, normal capacity/overhead allocation, rebates, returns, freight, WIP and negative-stock boundaries. | Define item/location/currency units, rounding level and movements-to-COS bridge.
methods.input_contract: Opening layers; receipts/issues; eligible costs; quantities; selected cost policy.
methods.independent_expected_work: Synthetic vector: 100 units at CU10 plus 50 at CU14, issue 120; FIFO issue CU1,280/closing CU420; periodic weighted average issue CU1,360/closing CU340 before policy rounding. Independently verify additional cases.
methods.unsupported_or_judgment: Weighted average timing matters; production costing cannot be claimed from a simple trading-stock formula. IAS 2 does not permit arbitrary method substitution.
methods.lead_role: Accounting/audit methodology analyst + owning domain engineer
methods.profile: Periodic weighted-average costing v1; separate additional profiles
methods.inputs: Opening quantity/value; approved eligible receipt/conversion cost; issues/closing quantities; cost method; recorded COS/closing value.
algorithm: Reconcile quantities before costing
Supported periodic weighted average =eligible cost available /units available; retain rational unit cost until declared issue-total rounding
Compute issue cost then residual closing value so total eligible cost reconciles exactly
Specific identification/FIFO/moving average/production overhead need their own profile when required; no silent conversion of all clients to weighted average
methods.judgment: Permitted cost formula, eligible cost, normal capacity, abnormal waste and policy consistency require reviewed basis.
methods.example: 10 units/100 CU +10/140 ->20 units/240,average12. Issues15 ->180 CU;closing5 ->60 CU.

methods.title: Inventory NRV and obsolescence indicators
methods.standards_to_verify: IAS 2; ISA 540, 500
methods.question: How are estimated selling prices and sale/completion costs corroborated?
methods.research_steps: Research item/group basis, postperiod sales evidence, damaged/obsolete stock, write-down and reversal conditions. | Specify approved estimates, completion/selling costs and lower-of-cost/NRV comparison. | Distinguish slow-moving flags from a supportable valuation conclusion.
methods.input_contract: Costed items; quantities; selling evidence; completion/selling cost assumptions; previous write-downs.
methods.independent_expected_work: Independent inventory with cost above/below NRV, partial sales evidence, negative estimated proceeds and constrained reversal.
methods.unsupported_or_judgment: No universal age bucket/write-down percentage; approved estimates and applicable policy remain necessary.
methods.lead_role: Accounting/audit methodology analyst + owning domain engineer
methods.profile: NRV input comparison and movement indicators
methods.inputs: Item cost/quantity; approved selling price; completion cost; necessary selling cost; observable evidence date; movement/age thresholds.
algorithm: Calculate approved NRV per unit =selling price -completion cost -necessary selling cost
Compare at supported item or justified grouping level; do not offset unrelated item gains and losses
Calculate proposed write-down =max(0,cost-NRV) xquantity under supported nonnegative scope
Flag slow/nonmoving items independently; review reversals subject to original write-down limit and current evidence
methods.judgment: Estimated selling price/costs, grouping, obsolescence and reversals require professional evidence; turnover alone is not NRV.
exceptions: Negative NRV requiring separate obligation analysis
methods.example: Cost12 CU,price11,completion1,selling1 ->NRV9;5 units ->write-down15 CU.

methods.title: Asset roll-forward, disposals and revaluation movements
methods.standards_to_verify: IAS 16, IAS 38, IAS 36; relevant IAS 40/IFRS 5 only if applicable
methods.question: Which cost, accumulated charge and carrying-value movements must reconcile?
methods.research_steps: Research additions, disposals, transfers, impairments, revaluations and held-for-sale changes by asset class. | Specify register-to-GL reconciliation, component identity and disposal gain/loss evidence. | Separate movement arithmetic from recognition, life/revaluation judgment and title inspection.
methods.input_contract: Asset/component register; opening balances; movements; disposal proceeds; accumulated charges; GL.
methods.independent_expected_work: Independent addition/partial disposal/transfer with cost and accumulated depreciation bridges; carrying value and GL reconcile separately.
methods.unsupported_or_judgment: A balanced asset register cannot certify asset existence, rights or correct capitalization.
methods.lead_role: Accounting/audit methodology analyst + owning domain engineer
methods.inputs: Asset/component identity; cost and accumulated charge openings; additions/disposals/transfers/revaluation; impairment; ledger.
algorithm: Reconcile gross cost and accumulated depreciation/amortization separately
Preserve disposal of original cost and related accumulated charge, not net carrying value only
Compute carrying amount after separately recorded impairment/revaluation effects
Reconcile movements/classes to ledger and evidence; retain actual disposal consideration and gain/loss support
methods.judgment: Recognition, revaluation class policy, derecognition date and classification remain human decisions.
exceptions: Revaluation across only selected class items
methods.example: Cost1000+add200-dispose100=1100;accum300+charge100-remove30=370 ->carrying730 CU before impairment.

methods.title: Depreciation and amortization
methods.standards_to_verify: IAS 16, IAS 38, IAS 8; selected policy
methods.question: Which method, component, service dates and estimate changes govern the charge?
methods.research_steps: Research straight-line, reducing-balance/units-of-production if applicable, components, residual value and available-for-use rules. | Specify daily/monthly conventions, leap years, disposals, idle/fully-depreciated assets, life changes and indefinite-life intangibles. | Separate prospective estimate changes from policy/error corrections and test floors/rounding.
methods.input_contract: Cost; residual; life; method; component; service/disposal dates; prior charge; policy version.
methods.independent_expected_work: Synthetic whole-year straight-line CU120 cost, CU20 residual, five-year life gives CU20 charge; separately test first/last periods, revised life and cumulative floor with independent schedule.
methods.unsupported_or_judgment: No automatic useful-life selection or tax-depreciation substitution; a formula passing does not approve capitalization.
methods.lead_role: Accounting/audit methodology analyst + owning domain engineer
methods.inputs: Cost/component; residual; useful life; available-for-use/disposal dates; reporting window; prior accumulated charge; actual days/month convention.
algorithm: Annual base =(cost-residual)/usefulLife for supported cost model
Apply approved actual eligible period convention; distinguish available-for-use from purchase/payment date
Cap charge to remaining depreciable carrying basis and retain over-depreciation as a separate exception
Finite-life amortization uses its own life/support; indefinite-life intangible is not mechanically amortized; estimate changes are prospective under reviewed basis
methods.judgment: Useful life, residual, consumption method, componentization, ready date and estimate revisions require actual review.
methods.example: Cost1000,residual100,life3 years ->annual300 CU. Approved half-year convention ->150 CU;remaining basis100 caps charge100.

methods.title: Capitalization, repairs and borrowing-cost support
methods.standards_to_verify: IAS 16, IAS 38, IAS 23; IAS 8 where relevant
methods.question: Which costs qualify and what evidence supports the chosen treatment?
methods.research_steps: Research directly attributable costs, development/research distinctions, replacements/components, decommissioning and borrowing-cost criteria. | Specify candidate screens as prompts for professional classification; define supported capitalization period and eligible amounts. | Identify conditional specialized assets/investment property and prevent silent adoption from keywords.
methods.input_contract: Cost lines; contracts; project stage; available-for-use facts; rates; management policy and evidence.
methods.independent_expected_work: Independent mixed repair/enhancement/development cost set with separately approved classification; calculation follows approved decisions.
methods.unsupported_or_judgment: Cost label, invoice size or successful depreciation cannot determine recognition; qualification stays human.
methods.lead_role: Accounting/audit methodology analyst + owning domain engineer
methods.inputs: Approved capitalization policy; transaction/category/date; asset/service evidence; qualifying-asset decision; borrowing costs and suspension intervals.
algorithm: Compare additions/repairs with explicit policy categories and thresholds as candidates only
Distinguish direct costs from routine servicing and unsupported internal-development costs
For a supported borrowing-cost schedule calculate eligible costs over actual qualifying active intervals, respecting available incurred costs
Suspend/stop per reviewed qualifying-asset facts; route complex financing or development to reviewed specialist schedules
methods.judgment: Recognition criteria cannot be replaced by a monetary threshold; qualifying development and asset-ready dates require evidence.
methods.example: 100000 CU qualifying expenditure xapproved6% x6/12 active year=3000 CU subject to applicable borrowing-cost cap and policy facts.

methods.title: Effective interest, borrowings and covenants
methods.standards_to_verify: IFRS 9, IFRS 7, IAS 23; IAS 1/IFRS 18 for presentation; contract covenants
methods.question: Which cash flows, fees, day counts and contract terms determine the schedule?
methods.research_steps: Research amortized cost/EIR versus contractual interest, fees/premiums, modifications, floating resets and impairment interactions. | Specify cash-flow timing, compounding, numerical solver behavior, day-count conventions and residual reconciliation. | Research covenant definitions, testing dates, waivers and presentation as separate contract/judgment questions.
methods.input_contract: Instrument contract; initial carrying value; contractual cash flows; fees; dates; rates; covenant definitions.
methods.independent_expected_work: Independent premium/discount/fee schedule and terminal balance; irregular periods, variable rates, no-root/multiple-root boundaries and covenant waiver timing.
methods.unsupported_or_judgment: A generic simple-interest or spreadsheet IRR result does not prove IFRS 9 correctness; covenant failure is not an automatic opinion.
methods.lead_role: Accounting/audit methodology analyst + owning domain engineer
methods.inputs: Facility contract; principal movements; coupon/day count; approved EIR/cash flows; fees; currency; covenant definitions/date.
algorithm: Reconcile principal separately from interest and fees
Contractual interest uses actual agreed balance/rate/day-count segments
For supported regular cash flows compute amortized-cost roll-forward opening+EIR interest-cash paid; solve EIR only with a bracketed unique-root contract and residual validation
Compute covenant headroom from exact signed definitions and test date; modifications/credit impairment/complex instruments route to separate approved profiles
methods.judgment: Classification, EIR inputs, modification/derecognition and covenant rights/waivers remain reviewed judgments.
methods.example: Principal1000 CU x12% x30/360=10 CU contractual interest. Opening AC950 x10% EIR -coupon80 ->closing965 CU.

methods.title: Lease liability and right-of-use schedules
methods.standards_to_verify: IFRS 16; applicable separate SME lease sections
methods.question: Which contract decisions and rates are required before recalculation?
methods.research_steps: Research lease identification/components, term/options, eligible payments, discount rate, exemptions and initial ROU costs. | Specify advance/arrears payments, modifications, remeasurement, index changes, incentives, impairment and disclosures for selected scope. | Separate lessee/lessor and sale-and-leaseback requirements; do not silently promise unapproved complex cases.
methods.input_contract: Approved lease facts; payment dates/amounts; rate and compounding; initial costs; term/options; amendments.
methods.independent_expected_work: Independent present-value and movement schedule with zero rate, advance rent, changed index, extension and termination; rate is synthetic/approved input, never a default law.
methods.unsupported_or_judgment: Lease term and incremental borrowing rate are judgments; periodic PV alone is not complete IFRS 16 compliance.
methods.lead_role: Accounting/audit methodology analyst + owning domain engineer
methods.inputs: Actual lease identification/term; dated fixed payments; approved discount rate; commencement; prepayments/incentives/direct/restoration costs; ROU life.
algorithm: Determine payment timing and exclude payments already paid at initial measurement
Liability =sum unpaid payments/(1+periodic rate)^period; preserve rate compounding convention
Roll liability by interest and actual payments; ROU opening includes applicable cost adjustments separately
Apply approved ROU depreciation period and retain impairment/reassessment/modification as separate supported method or reviewed work
methods.judgment: Lease definition, exemptions, options, rate, life and modifications require professional conclusions.
methods.example: Two year-end110 CU payments at10% annual ->initial190.91 CU. Year1 interest19.09/payment110 ->liability100.00 CU with declared rounding.

methods.title: Foreign-currency measurement and translation
methods.standards_to_verify: IAS 21, IFRIC 22; IAS 29 only if applicability requires
methods.question: Which currency, rate/date and measurement basis govern each transformation?
methods.research_steps: Research transaction recognition, monetary/nonmonetary closing treatment, settlements and presentation translation. | Specify rate direction, source/version, unavailable rates, lack of exchangeability, functional currency and intercompany differences. | Identify translation reserve versus profit/loss effects and historical rates; maintain transaction/functional/presentation amounts.
methods.input_contract: Amounts; currency roles; dates; rate source/direction; monetary classification; policy; rounding.
methods.independent_expected_work: Independent inverted-rate and mixed-currency vectors, historical versus closing rate and missing-date case; line-level bridge and separate FX effects.
methods.unsupported_or_judgment: No current market rate is assumed; average/closing/historical rates are not interchangeable; unknown rate cannot become 1.
methods.lead_role: Accounting/audit methodology analyst + owning domain engineer
methods.inputs: Transaction/functional/presentation currency; monetary classification; dated rate with direction; foreign amount; carrying amount; framework.
algorithm: Normalize explicit rate direction to functional units per foreign unit
Initial transaction amount =foreign amount xselected applicable transaction rate
Retranslate monetary closing balances at approved closing rate and compare carrying amount
Keep historical nonmonetary, fair-value-date, advance-consideration and foreign-operation translation profiles separate; no blanket closing-rate conversion
methods.judgment: Functional currency, monetary nature, rate accessibility and P&L/OCI classification require review.
methods.example: 100 foreign units at3 CU/foreign=300 CU initial;closing monetary rate3.2 ->320 CU,20 CU remeasurement difference before classification.

methods.title: Investment income and fair-value input review
methods.standards_to_verify: IFRS 9, IFRS 7, IFRS 13; IAS 28/IFRS 11 only if applicable; ISA 540, 620
methods.question: Which classification and valuation inputs can the system verify?
methods.research_steps: Research classification, quoted-price suitability, valuation dates, ownership/quantity, accrued income and fair-value hierarchy. | Specify approved price sources, model input provenance, units, FX and investment movement bridges. | Separate model arithmetic from fair-value technique/assumption approval and specialist work.
methods.input_contract: Holding quantities/rights; prices/valuation model; dates; source; accrued flows; classification decisions.
methods.independent_expected_work: Independent quantity × approved price plus approved adjustments, stale quote, corporate action and valuation sensitivity; specialist unsupported cases remain explicit.
methods.unsupported_or_judgment: A market quote does not automatically establish appropriate fair value; ownership/control and active-market judgments require evidence.
methods.lead_role: Accounting/audit methodology analyst + owning domain engineer
methods.inputs: Instrument/units; opening/trades; custodian evidence; prices/date/market/currency; income rights; approved classification and valuation method.
algorithm: Reconcile units/cost/transactions to custodian and GL without substituting custodian completeness for all holdings
Recalculate contractual dividend/coupon/simple yield inputs with exact dates and denominator
Compare supplied valuation inputs to their source/date and trace calculation
Complex fair-value models/classification/market assessment remain reviewed specialist work; quoted input is not an automatic fair-value conclusion
methods.judgment: Rights, classification, market activity, valuation technique and observable-input appropriateness require evaluation.
methods.example: 10 units xapproved50 CU=500 CU quoted-value calculation. Dividend2 CU per eligible unit ->20 CU; rights and valuation date still evaluated.

methods.title: Expected credit losses and allowances
methods.standards_to_verify: IFRS 9; ISA 540; selected SME requirements separately
methods.question: Which ECL model applies and what assumptions require approval?
methods.research_steps: Research simplified/general approach, lifetime versus 12-month ECL, credit risk/staging, discounting, forward-looking scenarios and data. | Compare provision matrix and PD/LGD/EAD implementations only for their approved portfolios and assumptions. | Specify scenario weights, segmentation, recoveries/collateral, write-offs, modifications and validation/sensitivity.
methods.input_contract: Exposure and cash-flow data; segments/stages; historical loss; forecasts; approved assumptions; discount basis.
methods.independent_expected_work: Independent small discounted scenario model and approved provision-matrix example; changed weights, missing data, credit-impaired asset and recoveries tested.
methods.unsupported_or_judgment: Aging × arbitrary percentage or PD×LGD×EAD alone cannot be advertised as universal IFRS 9 ECL.
methods.lead_role: Accounting/audit methodology analyst + owning domain engineer
methods.profile: Approved provision-matrix calculation + separately reviewed ECL models
methods.inputs: Eligible exposure/aging/segments; disjoint specific assessments; approved rates/scenarios/discounting; actual forward-looking support.
algorithm: Choose applicable general versus simplified impairment approach explicitly
For supported matrix calculate sum exposure xapproved lifetime loss rate, removing exposures separately assessed from collective double counting
For provided cash-flow/scenario model calculate probability-weighted discounted cash shortfalls with probability/unit/horizon checks
Reconcile allowance movements; review staging/SICR/default/forward-looking assumptions and model adequacy separately; twelve-month ECL is not twelve months of contractual shortfalls
methods.judgment: Scope, segmentation, rates, forecast adjustments, staging, collateral and model appropriateness require independent professional evaluation.
methods.example: Eligible exposures1000 CU at2% plus500 at10% ->allowance70 CU; separately assessed exposure must not also sit in either bucket.

methods.title: Nonfinancial asset impairment
methods.question: Which asset/CGU and recoverable amount inputs are appropriate?
methods.research_steps: Research IAS 36 scope exclusions, indicators, annual tests, CGU/goodwill allocation and recoverable amount. | Specify approved cash flows, discounting, terminal assumptions, fair value less disposal costs and sensitivity. | Research impairment allocation/floors/reversals and future depreciation consequences; separate unsupported valuation judgments.
methods.input_contract: Carrying amount; approved CGU; cash flows; discount basis; disposal costs; allocation; prior impairment.
methods.independent_expected_work: Independent recoverable-amount comparison, CGU allocation and reversal cap; goodwill reversal denied; asset outside IAS 36 routed to proper standard.
methods.unsupported_or_judgment: No one impairment algorithm covers inventory, IFRS 9 assets and goodwill; valuation assumptions require practitioner/specialist approval.
methods.lead_role: Accounting/audit methodology analyst + owning domain engineer
methods.inputs: Correct asset/CGU scope; carrying amount; supported VIU and FVLCD; forecasts/rate; goodwill allocations; prior impairment.
algorithm: Separate IAS36 scope from inventory NRV and financial-asset ECL
For supported input comparison recoverable=max(VIU,FVLCD); loss=max(0,carrying-recoverable)
For a supported discounted model pin dates, pre-tax compatible cash flows/rate and terminal assumptions; require denominator/rate consistency and sensitivity
Allocate/reverse only under an explicit approved asset/CGU/goodwill profile; keep impairment facts and subsequent depreciation link
methods.judgment: CGU identification, forecast plausibility, discount/terminal assumptions, recognition and reversal limits require professional work.
methods.example: Carrying100 CU,VIU80,FVLCD90 ->recoverable90,loss10 CU. This comparison does not independently validate either valuation.

methods.title: Payroll, benefits and gross-to-net
methods.standards_to_verify: IAS 19, IAS 26 where applicable; verified Mongolian labor/tax/social-insurance law
methods.question: Which dated legal and contractual rules govern each component?
methods.research_steps: Research employee versus employer obligations, earnings/benefits, caps, exemptions, progressive brackets, prorating and effective dates. | Reconcile roster, payroll run, bank payments and GL; separate payroll taxes from IAS 19 benefit measurement. | Specify pay-period/annual cumulative behavior, off-cycle reversals, leave and personal-data access.
methods.input_contract: Employee terms; payroll categories; hours/dates; approved statutory rule pack; deductions; payments.
methods.independent_expected_work: Independent payroll examples around each verified threshold and period change, partial month and correction; no real employee identifiers in synthetic fixtures.
methods.unsupported_or_judgment: No tax/social-insurance rate from an old example becomes law; defined-benefit valuation may need a separately approved actuarial route.
methods.lead_role: Accounting/audit methodology analyst + owning domain engineer
methods.inputs: Employee/run/payment identity; employment/earnings data; approved dated tax/social-insurance brackets/caps/reliefs; benefits obligations.
algorithm: Reconcile authorized roster, gross payroll, deductions, bank payments and GL by run
Calculate each earnings/deduction component under explicit dated basis/brackets/caps; separate employee from employer costs
Reconcile gross-deductions=net and employer liabilities separately
Review leave/bonus/accrual obligations; actuarial defined-benefit work remains separately evidenced; rates are never inferred from this example
methods.judgment: Employment validity, benefit classification, taxable base, relief and local legal parameters require authority and actual review.
methods.example: Fictional gross1000 CU,approved deductions100+50 ->net850 CU. Employer contribution is not subtracted again from employee net.

methods.title: VAT and withholding reconciliation
methods.standards_to_verify: Verified applicable Mongolian tax law, regulations and tax authority guidance; ISA 250, 500
methods.question: Which taxable base, recognition date and return lines apply?
methods.research_steps: Retrieve primary provisions for VAT/withholding scope, rates, exemptions, credits, currency, dates and filing corrections. | Specify sales/purchase/GL/return bridges, credit notes, reverse/withholding cases and unavailable tax evidence. | Research rates at transaction/return period; distinguish tax-law calculation from accounting presentation.
methods.input_contract: Tax rule version; taxable transactions; invoice/return/GL; exemptions; credits; FX/date basis.
methods.independent_expected_work: Independent legal example or independently computed vector for every approved rate/bracket/exception; reconciliation exposes timing/permanent differences.
methods.unsupported_or_judgment: This plan approves no Mongolian tax rates; statutory lookup remains open until primary-source verification.
methods.lead_role: Accounting/audit methodology analyst + owning domain engineer
methods.inputs: Transaction/register/return/GL IDs; approved tax regime/rate/base; inclusion convention; deductible status; period; payments/credits.
algorithm: Calculate tax-exclusive base xrate or tax-inclusive gross xrate/(1+rate) explicitly
Apply dated eligibility/rounding/exemption rules and retain unsupported legal classifications
Reconcile registers to filed return, GL liability and payments with identified timing adjustments
Separate VAT from withholding, reversals and recoverability; discrepancies become investigation cases
methods.judgment: Applicable rate, taxable event, deduction/exemption and filing obligations are legal/accounting decisions with actual dated authority.
methods.example: Fictional10%:gross110 CU ->base100,tax10. This is an arithmetic fixture, not a Mongolian VAT-rate claim.

methods.title: Current and deferred income tax
methods.standards_to_verify: IAS 12, IFRIC 23; verified income-tax law; selected SME requirements separately
methods.question: How do taxable profit, tax bases and recoverability support the provision?
methods.research_steps: Research current tax bridge, temporary/permanent differences, enacted/substantively enacted rate and tax-loss/credit evidence. | Specify taxable/deductible differences, reversal timing, recognition exceptions, uncertain treatments, offset/presentation and OCI/equity effects. | Assess special rules such as Pillar Two only if entity/scope requires; separate deferred tax arithmetic from recognition judgment.
methods.input_contract: Accounting/tax bases; law/rates/dates; tax return bridge; forecasts; loss expiry; approved recognition.
methods.independent_expected_work: Independent asset/liability temporary-difference examples, changed rate, loss and recognition constraint with synthetic assumptions; recoverability conclusion stays human.
methods.unsupported_or_judgment: A flat rate times accounting profit is not complete current/deferred tax; no generic DTA recognition from a positive number.
methods.lead_role: Accounting/audit methodology analyst + owning domain engineer
methods.inputs: Accounting profit; approved permanent/timing adjustments; tax base/carrying values; enacted/substantively enacted rates; recognition evidence; return/GL.
algorithm: Bridge accounting to taxable profit with each adjustment identified and approved
Calculate current tax/credits under selected law pack and reconcile return/payments
Calculate temporary differences and schedule reversals/rates; keep asset/liability sign/classification explicit
Recognize DTA only under reviewed criteria and retain exceptions/offset/uncertainty/PillarTwo decisions in separate supported records
methods.judgment: Tax law, temporary versus permanent differences, recognition, rate on recovery/settlement and offsetting require actual review.
methods.example: Fictional taxable temporary difference200 CU x20% ->DTL40 CU if applicable. Permanent difference does not create deferred tax.

methods.title: Equity, reserves and dividends
methods.standards_to_verify: IAS 32, IAS 10, IAS 1/IFRS 18; applicable company law and authorizations
methods.question: What is accounting classification versus legal entitlement/authorization?
methods.research_steps: Research instrument terms, contribution/issuance, reserves, dividend declaration dates, treasury shares and distributability law. | Specify opening/movement/closing and cash/equity/GL reconciliation with source resolutions. | Separate equity/liability classification and valid authorization from register arithmetic.
methods.input_contract: Instrument register; opening equity; resolutions; dates; payments; shareholder/ownership facts.
methods.independent_expected_work: Independent contribution/dividend/treasury movement, postperiod dividend, unauthorized proposal and foreign currency cases.
methods.unsupported_or_judgment: A board resolution upload alone does not prove legal validity; dividends after period date need applicable IAS 10 treatment.
methods.lead_role: Accounting/audit methodology analyst + owning domain engineer
methods.inputs: Share/class/holder; opening capital/reserves/retained earnings; approved issues/buybacks/dividends/transfers; legal evidence; GL.
algorithm: Reconcile each equity component separately with signed movements
Recalculate shares xnominal/premium under actual instrument terms
Link each capital/distribution action to actual resolution/rights and posting evidence
Keep retained earnings/OCI transfers and subsequent-declared dividends distinct from reporting-date liabilities
methods.judgment: Liability-versus-equity classification, lawful distribution, treasury shares and authorization require professional/legal work.
methods.example: Retained earnings500 CU +profit100 -approved dividend40 +approved transfer10 =570 CU; other component carries opposite transfer10.

methods.title: Consolidation and intercompany eliminations
methods.standards_to_verify: IFRS 10, IFRS 3, IAS 21; IFRS 11/12, IAS 27/28 as applicable; ISA 600
methods.question: Which entities, dates and transformations belong in the group result?
methods.research_steps: Research control/scope decisions, component periods/policies, acquisition/disposal, ownership/NCI and group-audit responsibilities. | Specify intercompany matching, dividends, balances, unrealized profit, tax effects and approved elimination entries. | Separate financial-statement aggregation, currency translation and group-audit materiality/evidence; retain residual mismatches.
methods.input_contract: Approved scope/ownership; component TBs/policies; FX; intercompany details; acquisition facts; eliminations.
methods.independent_expected_work: Independent two-entity balance and unrealized-profit case plus minority ownership/foreign component; each elimination applied once and unexplained mismatch retained.
methods.unsupported_or_judgment: Ownership percentage alone does not determine control; a consolidating spreadsheet does not perform ISA 600 responsibilities.
methods.lead_role: Accounting/audit methodology analyst + owning domain engineer
methods.profile: Component aggregation and explicit eliminations v1
methods.inputs: Approved group/control scope; mapped aligned component TBs; currencies/translation; ownership facts; signed elimination journals; reciprocal balances.
algorithm: Retain each component original/mapping/translation independently
Aggregate only compatible mapped amounts
Apply approved balanced elimination journals once and reconcile unmatched reciprocal balances separately
Keep acquisition/NCI/goodwill/unrealized-profit/equity-method work as separately approved schedules rather than plug differences
methods.judgment: Control, acquisition date, ownership, consolidation policy, impairment and elimination basis require actual review.
methods.example: A receivable100 CU/B payable95 CU ->5 CU mismatch. Do not automatically erase100 on both sides or create a5 CU plug.

methods.title: Provisions, commitments and contingencies
methods.standards_to_verify: IAS 37; ISA 501, 540, 620; applicable legal evidence
methods.question: What recognition, measurement and disclosure judgments are needed?
methods.research_steps: Research present/legal/constructive obligation, probability, reliable estimate, expected-value/best-estimate approaches and discounting. | Specify provision movement, reimbursements, onerous contracts, contingent assets/liabilities and evidence changes. | Separate lawyer assessment, management estimate and auditor evaluation; preserve disagreements.
methods.input_contract: Matter facts; legal replies; probabilities/cash flows; discount basis; dates; reimbursements; judgments.
methods.independent_expected_work: Independent provision movement and approved estimate calculations; remote/possible/probable branches, disputed legal reply and missing range.
methods.unsupported_or_judgment: Litigation keyword or probability slider cannot automatically decide recognition; confidential legal evidence needs scoped access.
methods.lead_role: Accounting/audit methodology analyst + owning domain engineer
methods.profile: Provision/contingency register and structured estimate support
methods.inputs: Matter/obligation; event; legal/constructive basis; probability assessment; estimate/range; timing; discount/reimbursement; legal evidence.
algorithm: Capture obligation and recognition/disclosure assessment separately from numerical estimate
For approved large-population expected-value schedule sum probability xoutcome; a single obligation may require a different best estimate
Discount when applicable using compatible timing/rate and separate reimbursement asset basis
Reconcile opening+new+unwind-used-reversed=closing; unknown exposure remains unknown
methods.judgment: Present obligation, probability, reliable estimate, best estimate and disclosure are professional/legal conclusions; probability alone is insufficient.
methods.example: Approved outcomes0 CU at75%,100 CU at25% ->expected value25 CU for a suitable population model; not automatic recognition of a single lawsuit.

methods.title: Going-concern indicators and forecast scenarios
methods.standards_to_verify: ISA 570 applicable edition; IAS 1/IAS 8/IFRS 18 as applicable
methods.question: Which assessment horizon, forecast and evidence support the auditor's conclusion?
methods.research_steps: Research management and auditor responsibilities/horizons separately for pre/post-revised ISA 570 and actual reporting framework. | Specify cash-flow forecasts, financing commitments/covenants, sensitivities, mitigation feasibility and events beyond assessment period. | Define missing forecasts, contradictory assumptions, material uncertainty and report handoff with human conclusion.
